problem: Distributors run on manual purchasing, forecasting, order entry and inventory spreadsheets across ERP and email; Lark agents automate these with approvals and audit logs.
business_model: B2B SaaS for distributors; pricing not published

founders.name: Jason Wang
education: University of Toronto, Computer Engineering with minors in AI and Business
founders.background_notes: Launch post describes him as Datost co-founder and CTO.

founders.name: Michael Wang
education: NYU Stern, finance and management (left to start Lark)
founders.background_notes: Former Team Canada badminton player per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents integrating with many ERP systems and acting with spending limits need reliable integrations.

defensibility.rationale: ERP integrations and learned operating rules create some lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon expanded autonomous supply chain agents in 2026; not yet observable for Lark.

market_need_then: Site cites one customer, Interline Hardware, with 60 hours per week saved and 20 percent leaner inventory (company claims).

identity.logo: Black and white wordmark with a bird icon

brand_strength.rationale: Plain bird mark but shares its name with ByteDance's Lark and a YC billing startup.

outcome_analysis: Lark is a two person Fall 2026 company by a repeat YC founder, selling agents to distributors with one named customer and reported savings. There is no outcome yet. Name confusion with ByteDance's Lark is a real discoverability cost.
notes: Dealroom says $125K and Caplight $500,000 with Y Combinator, conflicting aggregators, unverified. Competitor search returned no dated named competitors, so the list is empty. A YC billing startup also named Lark exists. Founding year not stated on sources opened. Update: the round rests on a single database (Dealroom, 125K, undated); Caplight's 500,000 conflicts and is not recorded or summed. Searches found no press.
